title: fix(security)!: under a wall every environment-metadata write is the platform operator's, whatever its type (ADR-0131 D12 items 7–8, D11)
body:
Fixes #23231

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Execution of ruling A on #23231 (record 6145019463): under a wall, every environment-metadata write admits only the platform operator and `isSystem`. The one verdict, `walledCatalogWriteVerdict`, stops special-casing the security catalog, and no door pre-filters on the written type before asking it. `single` is unchanged.

The Clause-② value is measured: the diff adds no export, no error code and no response field. It removes one (`error.details.catalogItems` on the `install-local` refusal). `check:api-surface` is green.

## Step 1: measured first (BEFORE)

**Harness.** A booted `examples/app-crm` stack (`bootStack`, `multiTenant: 'posture-only'`, plus `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin`), with the same shape as W, W2 and W3:
- Organization A's owner holds an operator-authored set carrying `manage_metadata`, granted scoped to organization A (rung `TENANT_ADMIN`, `isPlatformAdmin: false`).
- Organization B's owner reads through `GET /meta`.
- Under `single`, A holds the set unscoped (rung `MEMBER`).

Measured on this branch at `bae5841bce`, before any code edit. `isolated` and `group` answered identically.

| Door (A, below the operator) | `isolated` | `group` | `single` | B reads afterwards (walled) |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `PUT /meta/object/:name` (create) | 200 | 200 | 200 | A's object |
| `PUT /meta/view/:name` (create) | 200 | 200 | 200 | A's view |
| `PUT /meta/flow/:name` (create) | 200 | 200 | 200 | A's flow |
| `PUT /meta/view/:name` over the operator's view | 200 | 200 | 200 | **A's label** |
| `POST /meta/view/:name/publish` of the operator's draft | 200 | 200 | 200 | **the draft, published** |
| `POST /meta/view/:name/rollback` of the operator's view | 200 | 200 | 200 | **the old version** |
| `DELETE /meta/view/:name` (reset) of the operator's view | 200 | 200 | 200 | **404** |
| dispatcher `PUT /meta/:type/:name`, a non-catalog type | admitted | admitted | admitted | (pinned by the then-control in `meta-walled-catalog-refusal.test.ts`) |
| `POST /packages` (create) | 201 | 201 | 201 | |
| `PATCH /packages/:id`, `/enable`, `/disable`, `POST /publish` | 200 | 200 | 200 | |
| `publish-drafts` on the operator's package | 200 | 200 | 200 | **the pending draft** |
| `revert`, `discard-drafts` | 200 | 200 | 200 | |
| `rollback`, `commits/:commitId/revert` | 200 | 200 | 200 | **the older commit** |
| `duplicate`, `adopt-orphans` | 200 | 200 | 200 | |
| `DELETE /packages/:id` | 200 | 200 | 200 | **404** |
| `install-local` install (a package carrying an object) | 200 | 200 | 200 | **A's object** |
| `install-local` upgrade of the operator's package | 200 | 200 | 200 | **A's label** |
| `install-local` uninstall of the operator's package | 200 | 200 | 200 | |
| `POST /automation` (flow create; not named by the ruling) | 200 | 200 | 200 | **A's flow** |

On the first harness run, `adopt-orphans` answered 403 under both walls. The environment then held the harness's own catalog orphan, so W3's catalog refusal fired. Once that set was saved into a package, the door answered 200; that second run is the one tabled.

**Verdict on the premise.** No named door was already closed. One organization's write reached every other organization at every door, so the refusal is owed at all of them. The data door to the ledger itself does not exist: `POST /data/sys_metadata` answered 405.

**The `organization_admin` assignment reading.** On the same harness, organization B's stock owner (`organization_admin`, rung `TENANT_ADMIN`) posted `POST /data/sys_user_permission_set`, under both walls. Every case answered **403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`** (object `sys_user_permission_set`):
- the `manage_metadata` set, to a member of organization B;
- the same set, to the owner's own user;
- a set carrying no capability, as the control.

The reason is the grant, not the capability: `organization_admin` is read-only on `sys_user_permission_set` and `sys_user_position` (`default-permission-sets.ts`). So a stock organization admin cannot hand out `manage_metadata`. An organization-scoped holder appears only through an operator's grant: an operator-authored set, a system write, or an operator-granted assignment-table grant or `adminScope` allowlist. This is a reading only, and the door refusal does not depend on it.

## The PM's mechanism hypotheses, measured

1. **Two layers of short-circuit: confirmed, plus a third shape.**
   - The verdict's own `isSecurityCatalogType` line (`meta-write-capability.ts`).
   - The REST `walledCatalogRefusal` pre-filter.
   - The dispatcher's `if (isSecurityCatalogType(type))` wrapper.
   - The `/packages` helper and `install-local` both asked the verdict for `SECURITY_CATALOG_TYPES[0]` and then refused only if the items read included a catalog type.
   - Every pre-filter is gone. The two package helpers no longer read items at all.
2. **#22447 closes these writes: disproved.** It retired the organization-scoped `manage_org_presentation` arm. A holder of `manage_metadata` itself passed every door (table above).
3. **The data door is out of reach: confirmed by reading.** `createWalledCatalogDataDoorRefusal` maps only `sys_position`, `sys_permission_set` and `sys_capability` to a type, and calls `next()` for every other object before asking the verdict. A wider verdict reaches no other data. It and the catalog gates in `security-plugin.ts` are not edited (seat 2's region).
4. **Ordinary members writing metadata in a product flow: none found.**
   - Every door here demands `manage_metadata` first: `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict`, `requireManageMetadata`, `install-local`'s `requireInstallCapability` and the `/automation` `refuseUngrantedFlowWrite`.
   - Its only stock holder is `admin_full_access` (`ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES`). `organization_admin` carries `manage_org_users`, `setup.access`, `setup.write` and `manage_mailboxes`.
   - Every registered metadata type is environment metadata: the 28 types of `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY`, from `object` to `skill`. Each is stored in `sys_metadata`, which carries no organization column (ADR-0131 D6/D7).
   - No user-scoped type exists. ADR-0131 D13 parks personal views as a future user-owned object, not as a `/meta` type.
   - So the refusal removes nothing an ordinary member could do. Under a wall it removes the organization-scoped `manage_metadata` holder only.
5. **Headquarters IT under `group`.** See the fork-clause reading below.

## The fork clause: what the repo says HQ IT holds

- **ADR-0131 D12 item 7:** "The metadata-authoring capability (`manage_metadata` / `studio.access`) is what headquarters IT holds and plant admins do not." It names the capability, not the posture rung. The same item calls every customization "environment-wide and operator-gated (D6)".
- **The posture ladder (`posture-ladder.ts`).** `PLATFORM_ADMIN` derives from the platform-admin anchors and never from a held capability. Under `group` and `isolated` the anchor is `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`, which `environment-variables.mdx` marks "Required under the walled postures". Holding `manage_metadata` never lifts the rung.
- **`delegated-administration.mdx`.** It says HQ is not constrained by delegation, and it does not say who holds `manage_metadata`.
- **Reference deployments.** No example runs `group`. The only `group` harnesses are the W family dogfood tests, where the platform operator is the seeded admin declared in `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`.

**Reading.** In a stock `group` deployment, HQ IT's `manage_metadata` comes from the platform-admin set, so HQ IT is the operator and keeps authoring. The ADR's own text, though, describes HQ IT as a `manage_metadata` holder without naming the rung. A deployment that gave HQ IT an operator-authored set granted inside the HQ organization has a non-operator HQ IT. Under this PR that HQ IT is refused every metadata write, and its administrators must be declared in `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`.

That is the operational consequence the ruling asked to surface. It is reported on #23231, the PR stays a draft, and `content/docs/deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx` now says it in the deployer's terms.

## What changed

- **`@objectstack/metadata-core`: `walledCatalogWriteVerdict`.**
  - The catalog-only line is gone, so every type is judged alike.
  - The message names the written type ("a position", "a permission set", "a capability", "a package", or "a 'view' metadata item"), the posture, and "ADR-0131 D3, D12 items 7–8, D11". It points at an environment of the organization's own.
  - The export's name is unchanged.
- **`@objectstack/rest`.** `walledCatalogRefusal` drops its pre-filter. The four `/meta` doors (save, reset, publish, rollback) refuse a non-operator `403 FORBIDDEN` for every type.
- **`@objectstack/runtime`.**
  - The dispatcher `PUT /meta` drops its catalog wrapper and answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`.
  - `refuseWalledCatalogPackageWrite` drops its item reading. All thirteen `/packages` write doors ask it right after `requireManageMetadata`, before any read or write. Its three item readers (`storedRowTypes`, `readCommitRow`, `commitItemTypes`) are deleted.
  - The `/automation` definition writes (create, update, delete, clone) ask the verdict through the new `refuseWalledFlowDefinitionWrite`. The enablement door keeps the ADR-0126 §5 activation gate.
- **`@objectstack/cloud-connection`.** `refuseWalledCatalogPackage` drops its catalog reading. `install-local` install, upgrade and uninstall refuse a non-operator `403 FORBIDDEN`.
- **Activation remedies (`activation-gate.ts`).** The flow, action and permission-set remedies recommended a clone or a sibling item. That refusal is answered only under a wall, where those writes are the operator's now (and for permission-set clones, since W). The remedies now name the operator.
- **`@objectstack/spec`.**
  - The ADR-0087 semantic entry `walled-environment-metadata-writes-retired`.
  - The W2 and W3 entries no longer claim that a catalog-free package is "handled exactly as before".
- **Docs.**
  - `deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx`: a postures-table row, and a section on who writes the environment's metadata and on HQ IT.
  - `api/metadata-api.mdx`: the `PUT /meta` and `/packages` rules.
  - `permissions/permission-sets.mdx` and `permissions/capabilities.mdx`.
  - Census row 55b in `permissions/system-context.mdx`, which now anchors `refuseWalledFlowDefinitionWrite` too.
  - The platform-checklist clause that quoted the action remedy.
- The ADR anchor for `meta-write-capability.ts`, and the changeset `.changeset/23231-walled-environment-metadata-writes.md`.

## Re-judged pins (the repo-wide sweep)

A tenant's write under a wall flips from 2xx to 403, so every pin that encoded the 2xx was flipped to assert the refusal and what did not move:
- `meta-walled-catalog-refusal.test.ts`: the "a type outside the catalog is not judged" control now asserts a refusal for an object, a view and a flow. It gains `isSystem` and operator controls.
- `automation-activation-posture-gate.test.ts`: the refusal no longer recommends a clone. The clone door refuses the tenant under a wall, with the walled sentence, not the activation one.
- `packages-vetted-org-source.test.ts`: the members are refused at every write door before any protocol call. The read doors are unchanged. A new operator arm keeps the "no organization is threaded" property for admitted writes.
- `packages-uninstall-refuse-before-mutate.test.ts`: the three non-operator callers are refused with nothing moved. The operator, with and without an active organization, uninstalls naming no organization.
- `packages-orgless-grants-capability-gate.test.ts`: the controls show that the capability gate admitted the member, and that the walled refusal answered next. The operator is the positive control.
- `meta-read-org-scope-parity.test.ts`: both transports refuse the ex-member under the wall. The operator's save lands env-wide on both.
- `wall-package-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` (W2) and `wall-package-doors-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` (W3): A's catalog-free CONTROL becomes a refusal pin. A can no longer create packages, so the "other package" arms use an operator-created package.

The refusal assertions of the catalog pins are kept verbatim. Message pins assert only what the message names: the posture, the ruling and the subject.

## Tests

All runs below are at head `824228ec35`, the merge of `origin/main` `5c9bfb0d3f`, unless noted.

- **New pins.**
  - `wall-environment-metadata-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`: 21 tests over `isolated`, `group` and `single`. It covers every door above, B's read-back, the operator controls and the `single` control.
  - `packages-walled-write-refusal.test.ts`: the 13 doors × 2 postures, with operator, `isSystem`, `single` and no-tenancy controls.
  - `automation-walled-definition-write.test.ts`: the 4 writes × 2 postures, with the same controls.
- **AFTER, on the BEFORE harness.**
  - Every walled door above answers 403: `FORBIDDEN` on REST `/meta` and `install-local`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` on `/packages` and `/automation`.
  - B reads the operator's version, unchanged.
  - `single` is unchanged, cell for cell. The operator control answers 200.
- **Suites.**
  - `@objectstack/runtime`, the whole package: 374 files, 6,178 passed, 19 skipped, in four runs (domains 116 files, plus 55, 100 and 103).
  - `@objectstack/rest`, the whole package: 284 files, 6,049 passed, 328 skipped, in two runs.
  - `@objectstack/metadata-core`: 18 files, 552 passed.
  - `@objectstack/cloud-connection`: 45 files, 693 passed.
  - `@objectstack/spec` `src/migrations`: 4 files, 208 passed.
- **Dogfood.**
  - The four wall files: 80 passed.
  - The eleven other walled dogfood files that write through these doors: 121 passed. They are `automation-toggle-tenant-scope`, `federated-anchor-provenance`, the four `install-local-*` files, `public-form-withdrawal-walled`, `schedule-acting-organization`, `security-catalog-showcase`, `showcase-public-form-redirect` and `showcase-public-form-walled-intake`. This run was before the merge, at `733500eb11`.
- **Typecheck.** `turbo run typecheck` for metadata-core, rest, runtime, cloud-connection, spec and dogfood: 71 of 71 tasks green. Runtime's `check:test-typecheck` covers its test files.
- **Lint.** It is narrowed, with all three pieces of evidence:
  - The population: `eslint.config.mjs` applies to `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}`.
  - The count: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 22 changed TS files gives 22 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
  - The invariance: the config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, per its own note), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- **Ablation, verdict leg.**
  - The catalog-only line was put back through `ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 → 0, blob `1fc932c81c` → `a6632971b2`.
  - metadata-core was rebuilt. `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in `dist/index.cjs` and `dist/index.js`.
  - Unit: 5 red, 10 green. Dogfood: all 16 refusal pins red (8 × 2 postures), with the 2 guards, 2 operator controls and the `single` control green.
  - Restore: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` is empty, the rebuild shows the marker absent from all 12 dist files, and the tree is clean.
- **Ablation, REST pre-filter leg.**
  - The first attempt was a no-op: the replacement contained the anchor, and the tool refused it (anchor 1 → 1) and restored. Nothing ran.
  - The second attempt put a catalog-only pre-filter in `walledCatalogRefusal`: anchor 1 → 0, blob `94317088f7` → `1512e81a2c`. rest was rebuilt, and the marker was found in `dist/index.cjs` and `dist/index.js`.
  - Dogfood: exactly the 10 REST `/meta` pins red (5 × 2 postures). The `/packages`, `install-local` and `/automation` pins and every control stayed green (11).
  - Restore: blob equals HEAD, the rebuild shows the marker absent, and the tree is clean.
- **Gates.** `dispatch-gates --commands` derives 122 commands; `--ran` accounts for all 122, 0 not measured.
  - 121 exit 0. `check:query-options-erasure` timed out under contention and passed on a rerun. `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` passed once the packages they read were built.
  - `check:platform-checklist` exits 1 with 8 ABSENT SYMBOL problems in `access-security.json`, `attachments-storage.json` and `search.json`. The identical 8 reproduce on `origin/main` `404fc477e5`. This diff's checklist edit (`api-backend.json`) is not among them.
  - The battery started at the merge commit `e7fdcc48e2`. It finished on `824228ec35`, whose only change is a test budget in the new dogfood file. The first 60 commands were rerun on `824228ec35` (see the report on #23231).

## Acceptance notes

- **Growth beyond the claim's file surface, named.**
  - `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`: the `/automation` definition writes. These doors were measured (200, and B reads A's flow), and leaving them open would make this PR's claim false. The bounded in-place fix holds: same defect class, the same one-call shape, no other claim on the file, the same gate family.
  - `activation-gate.ts`: its remedies were made false by this change.
  - The W2 and W3 migration entries, made false by this change.
  - `deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx`.
  - The platform-checklist clause.
- **Not walled here: `POST /meta/_migrate-stored`** (both transports). It is an install-wide, meaning-preserving rewrite of stored rows into the current shape, and it defines nothing. It still admits an organization-scoped `manage_metadata` holder under a wall (measured 200). It is reported on #23231 for the seat to judge against the ruling's "every environment-metadata write".
- `@objectstack/cloud-connection` keeps its `@objectstack/objectql` dependency, which W2 added for the catalog reading this PR removes. No import of it remains. The dependency, the lockfile entry and the vitest alias are left as they are.
- The verdict keeps the name `walledCatalogWriteVerdict`, as do `walledCatalogRefusal`, `refuseWalledCatalogPackageWrite` and `refuseWalledCatalogPackage`. The security plugin's data door (seat 2's region) imports the export under that name.
- The data door is untouched. Since stage 8 retired the catalog row objects, it answers for no registered object.
